title: Inadvertent Global Variable Modifications (Namespace Pollution Side-Effects)
pattern: A function relies on a global variable to hold its return or state value, allowing subsequent calls to unrelated routines to inadvertently overwrite the variable's value.
why_bad: It introduces severe, non-obvious temporal side effects. A developer calling `get_other_answer` assumes it has no effect on `ans`, but because they share a hidden global namespace variable, the calculation is corrupted.
detection: Multiple functions write to and read from a single static/global mutable variable to pass intermediate results or return values.
fix:
Eliminate global storage for return values or intermediate states. Return values directly from functions as stack outputs.
```rust
// Values returned directly, removing global variable write.
```
source: *Code Complete* by Steve McConnell (Chapter 13, "Inadvertent changes to global data", "Visual Basic Example of a Side-Effect Problem").
